extracted: The authors use receptor availability (non-displaceable binding potential), an indirect measure, instead of 'occupancy', which they call misleading and not measurable directly in people; a fall in availability is proportional to a rise in occupancy only if receptor affinity and endogenous opioid levels are constant. Measures taken 4 hours after the daily dose, the earliest post-dose time studied, probably reflect less than the largest fall in availability; within-day PET time courses are not feasible. There is no gold-standard definition of clinically meaningful blockade, and neither the availability needed for withdrawal suppression or blockade nor how it varies with patients, opioids and routes is known.
